notes: Lower-mid front vowel /ɛ/ of the northern dialect, written e like /e/: /pel/ 'to steer' : /pɛl/ 'to be in a taboo relationship', /ser/ : /sɛr/ (p. 40). The only vowel found word-finally of the two; /e/ does not occur finally (p. 41). The contrast is absent in the Kiti dialect and 'there is some reason to believe that the contrast between /e/ and /ɛ/ is predictable' in the northern dialect (p. 41). Rehg (1984) has one mid front vowel with [e] and [ɛ] allophones (decision rehg1981-e).
Long /ɛ/: ne 'to be distributed' : neh 'its leg' (p. 43). All vowels occur long; length is phonemic (p. 43).
